$comment: PRD registry — source of truth for ticket metadata, dependencies and resource locks.
npm run prd:board   human-readable lock board + exclusive-overlap matrix
npm run prd:check   exit 1 on any lock violation (used in CI and deploy)
npm run prd:sync    rewrite the generated lock banners, then re-check
Resource tokens are an EXCLUSIVITY namespace, not file globs. Two tickets that are
both in_progress and share an `exclusive` token is a hard error. File paths are too
noisy — every ticket touches index.js and schema.prisma — but migration folders,
middleware definitions and token claims genuinely cannot be edited by two branches
dependencies may point at a whole ticket ('0001') or a single phase ('0001#1B').
Phase granularity matters: 0003 unblocks when 0001#2 lands, not when all of 0001 does.

statuses.draft: being written; may be authored freely, must not be implemented
statuses.blocked: authored, waiting on another ticket or resource; MUST NOT be implemented
statuses.ready: all blockers clear; safe to start
statuses.in_progress: actively being implemented; holds its exclusive tokens
statuses.superseded: replaced by another ticket; set superseded_by
